_comment: Conformance vectors for deterministicSubject / deterministic_subject. Both the Swift leg (SubjectGeneratorTests) and the Rust leg (subject_generator.rs #[cfg(test)]) must produce the expected output for every case. Seed: 0xCAFEBABEDEADBEEF (not used by this algorithm — the function is purely deterministic on its input).

cases.description: Period followed by space triggers sentence boundary
cases.input: Harrow count survey north zone result: 12. Field crew verified the total.
cases.expected: Harrow count survey north zone result: 12.

cases.description: Question mark followed by space triggers sentence boundary
cases.input: What did the Harrow count survey record for the north zone? The answer was 12.
cases.expected: What did the Harrow count survey record for the north zone?

cases.description: Exclamation mark followed by space triggers sentence boundary
cases.input: Batch B14 lab test output: 74 units! Technician sign-off on file.
cases.expected: Batch B14 lab test output: 74 units!

cases.description: No sentence boundary — entire content returned
cases.input: user: Hello world how are you
cases.expected: user: Hello world how are you

cases.description: No sentence boundary with content exceeding 120 chars — truncated to 120
Period followed by digit is a decimal point, not a sentence boundary
cases.input: Station S-7 log: reading 1.8 m/s at 0800.  More info.
cases.expected: Station S-7 log: reading 1.8 m/s at 0800.

cases.description: Leading and trailing whitespace is stripped before extraction
Sentence boundary at end of string (no trailing whitespace or text)
Period followed by newline is a sentence boundary

CRLF pairs are normalized to spaces BEFORE the 120 cap, so the emitted subject can never exceed the contract after per-scalar newline replacement (regression: LongMemEval-m question 8b9d4367, 123 chars)
